types.name: Fenrir::AdditiveReference
types.doc: What an additive layer's clip is measured from (ADR-0036).

values.name: ClipStart
values.doc: The clip's own pose at time 0, rest where the clip is silent: the default.

types.name: Fenrir::AssetHandle<Fenrir::Clip>
types.doc: Names one asset of kind `T` (`Mesh`, `Image`, `Material`, `Shader`, `Model`, `Skeleton`, `Clip` or `BoneMask`) in the asset store: a slot index plus the generation the slot had when the asset was made (ADR-0021). Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. Once the asset is freed the slot's generation moves on and the handle is stale: it no longer resolves, and users skip it. A default-made handle is empty and never resolves.

types.name: Fenrir::ClipEventId
types.doc: A short number for a clip event's name: the 32-bit FNV-1a hash of its UTF-8 bytes. A convenience for comparing names cheaply; an event is identified by its index and its clip's revision, never by this.

types.name: Fenrir::Entity
types.doc: Entity class that is used to interact with the entity list. This forms the basis of the ECS

types.name: Fenrir::AnimationEvent
types.doc:
An animation event (ADR-0034): sent from the `Animate` stage when a playback cursor crosses one of its clip's timed events. Read it with an `EventReader<AnimationEvent>`: a `PostUpdate` reader that runs after the pose pipeline sees it the same frame, an `Update` reader the next frame.

Forward playback crosses the events in (previous, current], reverse playback those in [current, previous), in playback order, every lap of a wrap included; when playback starts, the event at its starting boundary is crossed too. Seeks, clip changes, pauses, a speed of 0 and recovery from an unavailable clip cross nothing. Delivery is best-effort: at most `AnimationConfig::maxEventsPerInstancePerFrame` are sent per skeleton per frame, the earliest, and the rest are counted in one `AnimationEventsDropped`. A tick-posed skeleton's events (ADR-0040) are sent per tick, from that tick's `PreTick`, with the budget per tick: a `Tick` reader sees them in the tick that crossed them.

fields.name: skeleton
fields.doc: The skeleton entity whose playback crossed the event.

fields.name: layer
fields.doc: The layer that played the clip: the skeleton entity for its `Animator`.

fields.name: clip
fields.doc: The clip.

fields.name: clipRevision
fields.doc: The clip's revision when the event was crossed: `index` names an event only in this revision.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: The event's index in the clip's event list.

fields.name: nameId
fields.doc: The id of the event's name, for comparing names cheaply.

fields.name: time
fields.doc: The event's authored time, in seconds.

fields.name: loop
fields.doc: The lap the crossing happened in: the playback's completed loops at that moment.

types.name: Fenrir::AnimationEventsDropped
types.doc: Sent from the `Animate` stage when one frame's playback crossed more clip events than the budget lets through (ADR-0034): how many were crossed and not sent. The drop is also logged, once per skeleton instance.

fields.name: skeleton
fields.doc: The skeleton entity.

fields.name: layer
fields.doc: The layer that played the clip: the skeleton entity for its `Animator`.

fields.name: clip
fields.doc: The clip whose events were dropped.

fields.name: dropped
fields.doc: How many crossings were not sent, saturating at the largest `uint64_t`.

types.name: Fenrir::AssetHandle<Fenrir::BoneMask>
types.doc: Names one asset of kind `T` (`Mesh`, `Image`, `Material`, `Shader`, `Model`, `Skeleton`, `Clip` or `BoneMask`) in the asset store: a slot index plus the generation the slot had when the asset was made (ADR-0021). Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. Once the asset is freed the slot's generation moves on and the handle is stale: it no longer resolves, and users skip it. A default-made handle is empty and never resolves.

types.name: Fenrir::ClipLoop
types.doc: What a clip does at its boundary (ADR-0034).

values.name: Loop
values.doc: Wraps to the other end, however many laps one step covers.

values.name: Once
values.doc: Clamps at the end, or at 0 in reverse, holds that pose and is finished.

types.name: Fenrir::FadeCurve
types.doc: How a crossfade's progress becomes its blend weight (ADR-0036).

types.name: Fenrir::LayerMode
types.doc: How an animation layer combines with the pose beneath it (ADR-0036).

values.name: Override
values.doc: Blends toward the layer's clip: translation and scale lerp, rotation nlerps along the shortest arc. Channels the clip does not animate pass through.

values.name: Additive
values.doc: Adds the clip's difference from its reference pose onto the pose beneath. Channels the clip does not animate add nothing.

types.name: Fenrir::AnimationLayer
types.doc:
An animation layer (ADR-0036): plain data on any entity, playing a clip over the skeleton entity `skeleton` after its base `Animator`. Game code writes every field and FenrirAnimation never writes any; the layer's cursors, fade and caches are FenrirAnimation's (read them with `Animation::Playback(scene, layer)`, move the cursor with `Animation::Seek(scene, layer, seconds)`).

A skeleton's layers apply in sequence, by `order` then entity, each at an effective weight of `weight × mask weight(bone)` clamped to [0, 1], with nothing normalised. A layer with no base `Animator` layers over the skeleton's retained base pose. The clock and fade fields work as the `Animator`'s do; a weight of 0 removes the layer's effect and silences its events but never stops its clock.

fields.name: skeleton
fields.doc: The skeleton entity it layers onto; it need not be the layer's ECS parent.

fields.name: order
fields.doc: Where it applies among the skeleton's layers: after the base `Animator`, by order, then by entity.

fields.name: weight
fields.doc: How much of it shows, clamped to [0, 1]. Never touches its clock.

fields.name: mode
fields.doc: Override or Additive.

fields.name: mask
fields.doc: The bones it reaches, by engine name; empty reaches every bone at 1.

fields.name: reference
fields.doc: What an additive clip is measured from; ignored by override layers.

fields.name: clip
fields.doc: The clip to play; empty contributes nothing.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: Seconds of clip per second of frame time: negative plays in reverse, 0 holds.

fields.name: loop
fields.doc: Whether the clip wraps or clamps at its boundary.

fields.name: playing
fields.doc: False freezes the cursor and any running fade; the pose is still sampled there.

fields.name: fadeSeconds
fields.doc: How long a clip change crossfades, in seconds; 0 cuts.

fields.name: fadeCurve
fields.doc: The crossfade's curve.

types.name: Fenrir::Animator
types.doc:
The animator (ADR-0034): plain data on a skeleton entity naming the clip to play, how fast and in which direction, its loop mode and whether it plays. Game code writes every field and FenrirAnimation never writes any; it holds no time, because the playback cursor is FenrirAnimation's (read it with `Animation::Playback`, move it with `Animation::Seek`).

While `clip` names a clip, FenrirAnimation owns the skeleton's whole base pose: each frame it starts from the rest pose and applies the clip's channels. With no `Animator`, or an empty `clip`, the base pose is left alone. Changing `clip` restarts playback, at 0 or, with a negative `speed`, at the clip's duration, and crossfades from the outgoing clip over `fadeSeconds` (ADR-0036): the outgoing clip keeps playing on its own cursor, a change during a fade fades on from a snapshot of the blended pose, and 0 cuts. From no clip it fades from the retained base pose; to no clip it cuts, leaving the pose as last sampled. It is the skeleton's base animation layer: a full override, always first, under any `AnimationLayer`s.

fields.name: clip
fields.doc: The clip to play; empty plays nothing and leaves the base pose alone.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: Seconds of clip per second of frame time: negative plays in reverse, 0 holds.

fields.name: loop
fields.doc: Whether the clip wraps or clamps at its boundary.

fields.name: playing
fields.doc: False freezes the playback cursor; the pose is still sampled there.

fields.name: fadeSeconds
fields.doc: How long a clip change crossfades, in seconds, by unscaled frame time, frozen while paused; 0 cuts. A change during a fade applies to the next clip change.

fields.name: fadeCurve
fields.doc: The crossfade's curve: its weight as a function of progress.

types.name: Fenrir::ClipFinished
types.doc: Sent once, from the `Animate` stage, when a `ClipLoop::Once` clip reaches its boundary: each time its playback becomes finished (ADR-0034).

fields.name: skeleton
fields.doc: The skeleton entity.

fields.name: layer
fields.doc: The layer that played the clip: the skeleton entity for its `Animator`.

fields.name: clip
fields.doc: The clip that finished.

types.name: Fenrir::MaskScope
types.doc: Whether a bone mask entry covers one bone or the bone and everything below it.

types.name: Fenrir::PoseState
types.doc: Whether a skeleton entity's pose can be read (ADR-0031).

values.name: Ready
values.doc: Its skeleton asset resolves and its pose is built: reads give the current pose.

values.name: Unavailable
values.doc: Its `SkeletonPose` names an empty or stale skeleton: reads are empty until it resolves.

values.name: Missing
values.doc: It is dead, or has no `SkeletonPose`.

types.name: Fenrir::PlaybackInfo
types.doc: Where an animator's or a layer's playback stands, as `Animation::Playback` reads it.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: `Ready` while it plays (or holds) a clip on a `Ready` skeleton; `Unavailable` while the skeleton is not `Ready` or the clip handle is stale; `Missing` for an entity with no `Animator` or `AnimationLayer`, or a layer whose `skeleton` is no skeleton entity.

fields.name: time
fields.doc: The current clip's playback cursor, in seconds: in [0, duration]. An outgoing clip's is not shown.

fields.name: completedLoops
fields.doc: How many times playback wrapped, in either direction, since the clip started; saturating.

fields.name: finished
fields.doc: Whether a `ClipLoop::Once` clip has reached its boundary and holds there.

fields.name: fading
fields.doc: Whether a crossfade is running.

fields.name: fadeProgress
fields.doc: The running crossfade's progress in [0, 1], before its curve; 0 when none runs.
